St. Olga of Kwethluk

Saints

St. Olga of Kwethluk

St. Olga Michael · St. Matushka Olga · Arrsamquq

Period
1916–1979
Region
North America
Titles / vocation
Lay · Woman
Commemoration
October 27

Introduction

St. Olga Michael of Kwethluk is remembered as a Yup'ik mother, priest's wife, and midwife whose service centered on her Alaskan community. The OCA life recounts her care for families and people experiencing suffering. The official feast-day announcement fixes her commemoration on October 27, distinct from the November 8 civil date of her repose. Her modern glorification and published life are identified separately from earlier saints' narratives.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

St. Olga (Arrsamquq) was born in Kwethluk in 1916. She married Nicolai Michael, later an Orthodox priest. Her work included food preparation, sewing, and care for children.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “1916”

Life and notable events

She served as a midwife and helped people with material needs, especially women carrying grief or suffering from abuse. As a priest’s wife she was called Matushka. The church account also transmits later testimonies of healing encounters and dreams associated with her intercession.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “midwife”

Death and martyrdom

She died at home in Kwethluk on November 8, 1979, surrounded by family. Her death is not described as martyrdom. Her appointed feast day differs from her civil date of repose.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “November 8”

Writings and legacy

The OCA Holy Synod proclaimed her glorification in 2023. Her veneration centers a Yup’ik woman’s family, parish, and village service within the history of Orthodox Alaska.

[2] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · Holy Synod proclamation, November 2023; recognition of Olga

The 2023 synodal proclamation is the official record of the decision to glorify Olga. It records the wider ecclesiastical recognition of a woman whose service was rooted in her Yup’ik household and village.

[2] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · Holy Synod proclamation published 9 November 2023

The OCA’s report of the actual glorification describes clergy and pilgrims reaching Kwethluk by air to Bethel and then by boat. On June 19, 2025, a final memorial service at Olga’s grave preceded the procession of her relics to Saint Nicholas Church. The proclamation was read there, and the vigil followed; the Divine Liturgy was celebrated the next morning. Village residents hosted the visitors at their school. The celebrations then continued in Anchorage. This locates formal public recognition in the same village community in which she lived.

[3] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · OCA report dated June 21, 2025; Kwethluk procession, proclamation, and services · [2] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · Supplementary biographical record; anchor “2023”

Source context and historical limits

The identified source is a modern ecclesiastical life used in the Church’s commemoration. It transmits biographical material, received traditions, and—in some accounts—miracle narratives. Those claims remain attributed to this source; this app has not independently established a critical historical chronology or verified each miraculous episode. The OCA’s December 31, 2024 official announcement fixes the feast on October 27; this is distinct from the November 8 civil date of repose.

A concise navigation synopsis is necessary because full reproduction rights for this modern published life have not been established. Read its complete account at the identified source; the synopsis is not a quotation.

Text checked against the identified source. No theological review is claimed.

Dates reproduce the cited publication’s commemoration labels. They are not automatically converted civil dates. Some sources distinguish Old Style and New Style or record another local observance; check the individual context and your parish calendar.
